claims.text: The baseline catalyst is a nanoscale equiatomic PtPdRhRuIrOs solid-solution HEA.
Rh content will be increased by 10–20% relative to the equiatomic baseline while other metal fractions are reduced correspondingly.
Changing the HEA composition can modify the local electronic structure around active sites.
Rh enrichment shifts the local electronic environment of PtPdRhRuIrOs.
Rh enrichment promotes the formation and stabilization of isolated Pt/Pd sites.
Higher Rh content modifies the d-band center of the HEA.
Higher Rh content alters electronic interactions among the constituent metals.
Isolated Pt/Pd sites facilitate adsorption of ethanol and its intermediates.
Adsorption at isolated Pt/Pd sites favors the complete 12-electron pathway over a 4-electron pathway.
IrOsPtPdRhRu can catalyze ethanol oxidation through a 12-electron process, whereas the individual metals generally promote at most a 4-electron process.
Relative to the equiatomic catalyst, the Rh-enriched catalyst will have greater selectivity for complete 12-electron ethanol oxidation.
Greater 12-electron selectivity will be observable as increased conversion of ethanol to carbon dioxide and water.
The proposed Rh-selectivity relationship is expected to hold from room temperature to moderately elevated temperatures in conductive electrolytes.
The proposed relationship may not hold outside the nanoscale solid-solution regime.
The optimal Rh enrichment may depend on synthesis method and reaction conditions.
Failure of Rh-enriched catalysts to produce a statistically significant selectivity increase, or observation of decreased selectivity, would falsify the hypothesis.
